free_tier.stated: Reverse proxy makes an intranet public; hole punching supports TCP and UDP direct connection; aggregated links let one tunnel span several nodes. [translated]

egress.terms: The page title advertises daily free traffic without check-in, but no byte figure appears on the page body; the FAQ says relay-mode free users have a quota and P2P mode is unlimited in speed.; ingress: udp

interface_detail: Green-build Windows client download; no API or Linux client is described on the page.
chaining: A UDP-capable reverse proxy for a WG listener, with P2P as the fast path between a user's own devices.

limits.value: relay mode quota for free users, amount unpublished
P2P requires both ends in the same room

binding_note: No byte figure is published, so the relay quota is the only metered thing and its size is unknown; P2P mode avoids the relay but cannot serve an arbitrary public client, so it does not answer the ingress test.

identity_cost.detail: A downloadable client and a QQ group for support; no registration flow is described on the page read.

reliability_note: P2P fails on symmetric NAT and falls back to the metered relay; the vendor recommends the proxy when the room join fails.
confidence_note: The UDP hole punching and the relay quota statement are on the vendor page today; the daily traffic figure in the page title has no number behind it.

evidence.proved: TCP and UDP hole punching, reverse proxy, aggregated links; FAQ says P2P is not speed-limited and relay has a free quota

notes: The only provider in the sweep that pairs hole punching with a public reverse proxy, which matters because hole punching alone never gives a stranger a port. Closed source and supported through a QQ group, so durability is unproven.

extras.wg_detail: The FAQ says P2P mode is not speed-limited and relay mode gives free users a quota; a WG datagram can be carried on a UDP tunnel, but P2P direct connection reaches only peers that joined the same room, not arbitrary internet clients.
extras.volume_stated: The page title advertises daily free traffic without check-in, but no byte figure appears on the page body; the FAQ says relay-mode free users have a quota and P2P mode is unlimited in speed.
extras.transit_note: Relay nodes carry proxied traffic; direct P2P carries its own.
